title: UP BOARD CLASS 10 — Chemistry | Periodic Classification Elements

questions.question: Who among the following proposed the Modern Periodic Law, stating that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic number?

options.explanation: Dmitri Mendeleev proposed the Periodic Law based on atomic masses, not atomic numbers.
John Newlands proposed the Law of Octaves, an early classification of elements.
J.W. Dobereiner proposed the Law of Triads, grouping elements in sets of three.
Henry Moseley proposed the Modern Periodic Law in 1913, based on atomic numbers.

questions.explanation: Henry Moseley, in 1913, demonstrated that atomic number is a more fundamental property than atomic mass, leading to the Modern Periodic Law.
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: How many periods are there in the Modern Periodic Table?

options.explanation: There are 8 groups in the Modern Periodic Table, not periods.
The Modern Periodic Table consists of 7 periods.
There are 18 groups in the Modern Periodic Table, not periods.
There are 18 groups in the Modern Periodic Table, not periods.

questions.explanation: The Modern Periodic Table has 7 horizontal rows, which are called periods.
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: Elements in the same group of the Modern Periodic Table have the same:

options.explanation: Elements in the same group do not necessarily have the same number of shells.
Atomic numbers are unique for each element and are not the same for elements in the same group.
Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons, leading to similar chemical properties.
Atomic masses vary even among elements in the same group.

questions.explanation: Elements within the same group (vertical column) have similar chemical properties because they have the same number of valence electrons.
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following elements has the largest atomic radius?

options.explanation: Lithium has a smaller atomic radius compared to Potassium.
Beryllium has a smaller atomic radius compared to Potassium.
Potassium has the largest atomic radius among the given options.
Calcium has a smaller atomic radius compared to Potassium.

questions.explanation: Atomic radius increases down a group and decreases across a period. Potassium is in Group 1, Period 4, making it larger than Li (Group 1, Period 2) and also larger than Be and Ca which are in Group 2. Among the given options, K is the largest.
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: An element 'X' belongs to Group 14 of the Modern Periodic Table. Which of the following elements will it most likely resemble chemically?

options.explanation: Aluminium belongs to Group 13, not Group 14.
Silicon belongs to Group 14, so it will resemble element 'X' chemically.
Nitrogen belongs to Group 15, not Group 14.
Phosphorus belongs to Group 15, not Group 14.

questions.explanation: Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties due to having the same number of valence electrons. Silicon (Si) also belongs to Group 14, hence it will chemically resemble element 'X'. Aluminium is in Group 13, Nitrogen and Phosphorus are in Group 15.
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: Arrange the following elements in increasing order of their metallic character: Na, Si, Cl, Mg, Al.

options.explanation: This is the decreasing order of metallic character, not increasing.
Magnesium is less metallic than Sodium, so this order is incorrect.
This is the correct increasing order of metallic character.
Silicon is more metallic than Chlorine, so this order is incorrect.

questions.explanation: Metallic character decreases across a period from left to right and increases down a group. All these elements are in Period 3. Moving from left to right: Na (Group 1, most metallic) > Mg (Group 2) > Al (Group 13) > Si (Group 14) > Cl (Group 17, least metallic). So, the increasing order is Cl < Si < Al < Mg < Na.
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: An element has an atomic number of 17. To which group and period does this element belong in the Modern Periodic Table?

options.explanation: The element has 3 shells, so it belongs to Period 3, not Period 2.
Group 17 corresponds to elements with 7 valence electrons, not Group 7.
The element with atomic number 17 is Chlorine, which belongs to Group 17 and Period 3.
The element has 7 valence electrons, so it belongs to Group 17, not Group 16.

questions.explanation: The electronic configuration of an element with atomic number 17 is 2, 8, 7. The number of shells (3) indicates it belongs to Period 3. The number of valence electrons (7) indicates it belongs to Group 17 (for p-block elements, Group number = 10 + valence electrons).
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following elements would form the most basic oxide?

options.explanation: Silicon forms an acidic oxide (SiO₂).
Aluminium forms an amphoteric oxide (Al₂O₃).
Magnesium forms a basic oxide (MgO), but it is less basic than Sodium oxide.
Sodium forms the most basic oxide (Na₂O) due to its high metallic character.

questions.explanation: The basic nature of oxides increases with increasing metallic character. Metallic character increases down a group and decreases across a period. Among the given options, Sodium (Na) is the most metallic element (Group 1, Period 3), hence it will form the most basic oxide. Silicon forms acidic oxide, Aluminium forms amphoteric oxide, and Magnesium forms a basic oxide, but less basic than Sodium.
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: **Assertion (A):** Atomic radius generally decreases across a period from left to right. **Reason (R):** As one moves across a period, the nuclear charge increases, pulling the electrons closer to the nucleus.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: R is the correct explanation for A.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: The reason is also true.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: The assertion is true; atomic radius decreases across a period. The reason is also true and correctly explains the assertion. As the atomic number increases across a period, the number of protons (nuclear charge) increases, while the electrons are added to the same shell. This increased nuclear attraction pulls the electron cloud closer to the nucleus, resulting in a decrease in atomic radius.
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: An element 'M' forms an oxide with the formula M₂O₃. In which group of the Modern Periodic Table is this element 'M' most likely to be placed?

options.explanation: Group 1 elements form oxides with the formula M₂O, not M₂O₃.
Group 2 elements form oxides with the formula MO, not M₂O₃.
Elements in Group 13 form oxides with the formula M₂O₃, such as Al₂O₃.
Group 14 elements generally form oxides with the formula MO₂, not M₂O₃.

questions.explanation: In the oxide M₂O₃, oxygen has a valency of 2 (O²⁻). For the formula to be M₂O₃, the total negative charge is 3 × (-2) = -6. Therefore, the total positive charge from M must be +6. Since there are two atoms of M, the valency of M must be +3 (2 × +3 = +6). Elements with a valency of 3 typically belong to Group 13 (e.g., Aluminium, Al₂O₃). Group 1 elements have valency 1 (form M₂O). Group 2 elements have valency 2 (form MO). Group 14 elements generally have valency 4 (form MO₂).
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: The Modern Periodic Law states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their:

options.explanation: Atomic mass was the basis for Mendeleev's periodic table but not the Modern Periodic Law.
The Modern Periodic Law is based on atomic number as discovered by Henry Moseley.
Number of neutrons does not determine the chemical properties of an element.
Isotopic mass varies for isotopes of the same element and does not define periodic properties.

questions.explanation: Henry Moseley discovered that atomic number is a more fundamental property of an element than its atomic mass. The Modern Periodic Law is based on atomic number.
questions.hint: Consider what fundamental property Henry Moseley found to be crucial for the periodic table.

questions.question: Which of the following elements belongs to Group 1 (Alkali Metals) of the Modern Periodic Table?

options.explanation: Magnesium has 2 valence electrons and belongs to Group 2.
Calcium has 2 valence electrons and belongs to Group 2.
Sodium has 1 valence electron and belongs to Group 1 (Alkali Metals).
Aluminium has 3 valence electrons and belongs to Group 13.

questions.explanation: Sodium (Na) has an atomic number of 11, with an electronic configuration of 2, 8, 1. It has one valence electron, characteristic of Group 1 (Alkali Metals). Magnesium and Calcium are Group 2, and Aluminium is Group 13.
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

questions.question: As we move down a group in the Modern Periodic Table, the metallic character of elements:

options.explanation: Metallic character increases down a group due to larger atomic size and lower effective nuclear charge.
Metallic character does not decrease down a group.
Metallic character changes down a group.
Metallic character consistently increases down a group.

questions.explanation: Down a group, the atomic size increases, and the effective nuclear charge on the outermost electrons decreases. This makes it easier for the atom to lose electrons, thus increasing its metallic character.
questions.hint: Consider how atomic size and nuclear charge influence metallic properties.

questions.question: An element 'X' forms an oxide X₂O. In which group of the Modern Periodic Table is this element likely to be placed?

options.explanation: Group 2 elements have a valency of +2 (e.g., CaO).
Group 1 elements form X₂O oxides (e.g., Na₂O).
Group 13 elements form X₂O₃ oxides (e.g., Al₂O₃).
Group 14 elements form XO₂ oxides (e.g., CO₂).

questions.explanation: If the oxide is X₂O, it means element X has a valency of +1 (since oxygen has a valency of -2). Elements with a valency of +1 are typically found in Group 1 of the Modern Periodic Table (alkali metals).
questions.hint: Valency of +1 is characteristic of Group 1 elements.

questions.question: An element has an atomic number of 12. Its valency will be:

options.explanation: Valency of 1 is for elements with 1 valence electron (e.g., Na).
Magnesium has 2 valence electrons and a valency of 2.
Valency of 3 is for elements with 3 valence electrons (e.g., Al).
Valency of 4 is for elements with 4 valence electrons (e.g., C).

questions.explanation: The electronic configuration of an element with atomic number 12 (Magnesium) is 2, 8, 2. It has 2 valence electrons and tends to lose these 2 electrons to achieve a stable noble gas configuration. Therefore, its valency is 2.
questions.hint: Calculate the electronic configuration to determine the number of valence electrons.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct order of increasing atomic size for elements of Period 3?

options.explanation: This is not the correct increasing order.
Atomic size decreases across the period, so Si > P > S > Cl. The correct increasing order is Cl < S < P < Si.
This is the correct increasing order, but the question asks for a single correct option. Let's refine the options.
This is a decreasing order.

questions.explanation: In Period 3, atomic size decreases from left to right due to increasing nuclear charge. Sodium (Na) has the largest size, followed by Magnesium (Mg), Aluminium (Al), Silicon (Si), Phosphorus (P), Sulphur (S), Chlorine (Cl), and Argon (Ar).
questions.hint: Atomic size decreases across a period from left to right.

questions.question: The elements A, B, C, D have atomic numbers 9, 11, 17, 12 respectively. Which pair of elements belongs to the same group?

options.explanation: A is Group 17, B is Group 1.
B is Group 1, D is Group 2.
A and C both belong to Group 17 (Halogens).
B is Group 1, C is Group 17.

Group 1. Element C (atomic number 17): Electronic configuration 2, 8, 7. Valency 1 (non-metal). Group 17. Element D (atomic number 12): Electronic configuration 2, 8, 2. Valency 2 (metal). Group 2. Elements A and C both belong to Group 17 (Halogens).
questions.hint: Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons.

questions.question: An element 'E' is in Period 3 and Group 15 of the Modern Periodic Table. Which of the following statements about element 'E' is correct?

options.text: It is a metal and forms a basic oxide.
options.explanation: Group 15 elements are non-metals and form acidic oxides.

options.text: It has a valency of 5 and is a metal.
options.explanation: Group 15 elements have a valency of 3 and are non-metals.

options.text: It is a non-metal and its hydride would be EH₃.
options.explanation: Group 15 non-metals form EH₃ hydrides (e.g., PH₃).

options.text: It has 3 valence electrons and forms an ionic compound.
options.explanation: Group 15 elements have 5 valence electrons.

questions.explanation: An element in Group 15 has 5 valence electrons. It is a non-metal (e.g., Phosphorus). Non-metals generally form acidic oxides. With 5 valence electrons, it usually gains 3 electrons to achieve stability, so its valency is 3. Its hydride would therefore be EH₃ (like PH₃).
questions.hint: Group 15 elements have 5 valence electrons and form trihydrides (EH₃).

questions.question: Assertion (A): The atomic radius generally decreases across a period from left to right. Reason (R): As one moves across a period, the number of shells remains the same, but the nuclear charge increases, pulling the electrons closer to the nucleus.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: R is the correct explanation for A.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: R is true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: A is true.

questions.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true. The decrease in atomic radius across a period is precisely because the effective nuclear charge increases (due to increasing atomic number) while the number of electron shells remains constant. This increased pull on the valence electrons causes the atomic size to contract. Therefore, R is the correct explanation for A.
questions.hint: Consider how nuclear charge and electron shells influence atomic radius.

questions.question: An element 'X' has electronic configuration 2, 8, 7. It reacts with an element 'Y' that has 1 valence electron. The compound formed between X and Y is likely to have which of the following characteristics?

options.explanation: The compound is ionic, not covalent.
Ionic compounds are soluble in polar solvents, not non-polar solvents.
Ionic compounds have high melting points due to strong electrostatic forces.

options.text: Covalent, conducts electricity in molten state
options.explanation: The compound is ionic, not covalent. Ionic compounds conduct electricity in molten state or aqueous solution.

questions.explanation: Element 'X' (2, 8, 7) is a halogen (Group 17), a non-metal with high electronegativity, needing one electron to complete its octet. Element 'Y' has 1 valence electron, meaning it's an alkali metal (Group 1), a metal that readily loses one electron. The reaction between a Group 1 metal (Y) and a Group 17 non-metal (X) will involve the transfer of electrons, forming an ionic bond. Ionic compounds typically have high melting and boiling points, are soluble in polar solvents (like water), and conduct electricity in their molten state or aqueous solution, but not in solid state. Therefore, the compound formed will be ionic and have a high melting point.
questions.hint: Consider the nature of the bond formed between a metal and a non-metal.
questions.subject: upbo10-chemistry

options.explanation: This is incorrect because metallic character increases down a group.

questions.explanation: Metallic character is the tendency of an atom to lose electrons. As we move down a group, the atomic size increases, and the effective nuclear charge on the outermost electrons decreases, making it easier for them to lose electrons. Thus, metallic character increases down a group. As we move across a period, the atomic size decreases, and the effective nuclear charge increases, making it harder for atoms to lose electrons. questions.question: An element 'X' has an atomic number of 17. To which group and period of the Modern Periodic Table does it belong?

options.explanation: Period 2 is incorrect as Chlorine has 3 shells.
Group 7 is incorrect as the group is 17 for p-block elements with 7 valence electrons.
This is correct as explained above.
Both group and period are incorrect.

questions.explanation: The electronic configuration of an element with atomic number 17 (Chlorine) is 2, 8, 7. The number of shells indicates the period, which is 3 (K, L, M shells). The number of valence electrons indicates the group. Since it has 7 valence electrons and is a p-block element, its group number is 10 + 7 = 17.
questions.hint: Use the electronic configuration and the position of the element in the periodic table.

questions.question: Among the elements Li, B, C, N, and F, which element has the largest atomic radius?

options.explanation: Fluorine has the smallest atomic radius among these elements as it is the rightmost.
Nitrogen has a smaller atomic radius than Lithium but larger than Fluorine.
Carbon has a smaller atomic radius than Lithium.
Lithium has the largest atomic radius among these elements.

questions.explanation: All these elements (Li, B, C, N, F) belong to the same period, Period 2, of the Modern Periodic Table. Atomic radius generally decreases across a period from left to right due to an increase in nuclear charge, which pulls the valence electrons closer to the nucleus. Therefore, Lithium (Li), being the leftmost element in this series, will have the largest atomic radius.
questions.hint: Consider the trend in atomic radius across a period in the periodic table.

questions.question: Assertion (A): Elements of Group 18 are called noble gases. Reason (R): Elements of Group 18 have completely filled outermost electron shells and are chemically unreactive.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: This is correct as both assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: The reason is also true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true. Elements of Group 18 are indeed called noble gases. The reason for this nomenclature and their inert nature is their stable electronic configuration, specifically having completely filled outermost electron shells (octet or duplet for Helium). This stable configuration makes them chemically unreactive, hence 'noble' or 'inert.' Therefore, R correctly explains A.
questions.hint: Understand the definition of noble gases and their electronic configuration.

questions.question: Which of the following elements would exhibit the strongest electropositivity (metallic character)?

options.explanation: Magnesium is less electropositive than Strontium as it is higher in Group 2.
Calcium is less electropositive than Strontium as it is higher in Group 2.
Beryllium is the least electropositive among the given options as it is at the top of Group 2.
Strontium has the strongest electropositivity among the given options.

questions.explanation: Electropositivity (or metallic character) is the tendency of an element to lose electrons and form positive ions. This property increases as you move down a group in the periodic table because the atomic size increases, and the outermost electrons are farther from the nucleus, experiencing less effective nuclear charge. All the given elements (Be, Mg, Ca, Sr) belong to Group 2 (alkaline earth metals). Among them, Strontium (Sr) is located lowest in the group, meaning it has the largest atomic size and therefore the strongest tendency to lose electrons, making it the most electropositive.
questions.hint: Consider the trend in electropositivity down a group in the periodic table.
